review_reason: Focused SEG-Y/NumPy library; MIT licensed; meaningful adoption and current enough activity. Strong fit for the seismic data-tooling catalogue.
Highly relevant and recent, but primarily an educational/notebook collection rather than a reusable software package. Track maturity before catalogue promotion.
Modern SEG-Y I/O library with cloud/schema support; Apache-2.0; active in September 2026. Distinctive enough to complement segyio/segysak.
Technically relevant MIT-licensed research pipeline, but zero visible adoption and limited evidence of reusable package maturity.
Relevant FORCE-2020 well-log ML workflow, but currently looks like a research/notebook project with no license recorded and little adoption.
Broad academic project collection rather than a focused reusable geoscience software tool; low catalogue value relative to more mature alternatives.
Focused Julia SEG-Y I/O and seismic utilities; MIT license; actively maintained. Adds useful language/ecosystem diversity.
Relevant oil-and-gas data-science examples, but portfolio/learning orientation makes it weaker than a reusable technical library.
Clear modern use case: validated SEG-Y to MDIO/Zarr v3 conversion for AI/cloud workflows; Apache-2.0 and strong provenance/reproducibility positioning.
Interesting research/hackathon material, but old and inactive since 2022; better treated as research reference than an emerging maintained tool.
Useful recent petrophysics ML example with MIT license, but currently small notebook-scale project; monitor for packaging/documentation growth.
Petroleum-specific MCP server for LAS/well-log access; MIT licensed and directly relevant to PetroTechRadar's emerging AI/MCP coverage despite early-stage adoption.
Broad SEG-Y/SEG-D/SEG-2/SU desktop QC toolkit and very recent activity, but extremely new with minimal adoption; reassess after more releases/use.
Novel LLM-assisted SEG-Y header/parser concept, but no license is recorded and adoption is still minimal. Technically interesting, not yet ready for curated promotion.
Direct FWI relevance, but appears research/notebook oriented, inactive for about a year, with no license recorded and no visible adoption.

Distinctive MCP integration for OpendTect covering SEG-Y import and horizon tracking; MIT licensed and strategically relevant to agentic geoscience workflows. Early-stage status should be shown clearly.
Relevant native SEG-Y visualization/enhancement application with MIT license, but created only in September 2026 with very limited track record.
Useful remote seismic gather viewer with processing/QC features, but very new, minimal adoption, and no license recorded.
Relevant MATLAB/Octave SEG-Y utility with LGPL license, but tiny/new project and narrower value than established SEG-Y libraries.
Interesting PyTorch-aware SEG-Y I/O concept with GPL license, but currently very small and new; monitor for API/documentation maturity.
Ambitious browser petroleum engineering suite spanning many domains, but claims are broad, adoption is minimal, and no license is recorded in discovery metadata; requires deeper validation.
Interesting AI-assisted seismic compression stack with Apache-2.0 and recent activity, but zero visible adoption and performance/losslessness claims need validation.
Highly relevant carbonate/image-log application with DLIS input, but extremely new, one-star project and no license recorded. Strong candidate if it matures.
Relevant reproducible 2D seismic processing/QC implementation with MIT license, but appears case-study/research specific rather than a general-purpose package.
Relevant automated lithofacies ML pipeline with GPL-3.0, but no visible adoption and limited evidence yet of reusable package maturity.
